html-to-image 1.11.13 (MIT, license in html-to-image.LICENSE.txt), https://github.com/bubkoo/html-to-image
html-to-image.esm.js is its es/ build bundled into one file, so the page needs no build step (like three.module.min.js):
  npm pack html-to-image@1.11.13 && tar xzf html-to-image-1.11.13.tgz
  npx esbuild package/es/index.js --bundle --format=esm --minify --target=es2019 --outfile=html-to-image.esm.js
Loaded only when the Report popup's Visual feedback tab opens (site3d/scripts/feedback-capture.js).

One local change after the build (a canvas's picture became an <img> that waited for a decode and one animation frame, per canvas; on a busy 3D page on a slow phone that was
over a second, and the serialiser does not need the image loaded): in the bundle, function lt() is
  async function lt(t){let e=t.toDataURL();return e==="data:,"?t.cloneNode(!1):d(e)}
and is changed to
  async function lt(t){let e=t.toDataURL();if(e==="data:,")return t.cloneNode(!1);let n=new Image;return n.src=e,n}
A second one: in dt(), the loop over the style properties gets a hook, so the screenshot can leave out a declaration the clone does not need (it equals the element's default or
what the parent already gives it), which makes the picture's SVG several times shorter: after  let a=o.getPropertyValue(i);  insert  if(r.skipStyle&&r.skipStyle(i,a,t,o))return;
Redo these after any rebuild (the test in site3d/test/feedback.test.js reads the bundle and checks it).
